manual_steps: Langfuse moves to chart 2 (Langfuse 4) and starts with empty trace storage: traces, observations, scores and sessions recorded before this release are not carried over. Export any you need from the Langfuse UI before upgrading. Projects, users, API keys, prompts and datasets (kept in Postgres) stay.

Teams onboarded with --langfuse-secret: their per-team LiteLLM callback is the old 'langfuse' callback, which Langfuse 4 rejects. After the upgrade, add it again as 'langfuse_otel' (LiteLLM POST /team/<team_id>/callback, as in platform/config/kro/team-onboarding.yaml) and remove the old one. Platform-wide tracing needs nothing.

llm-d models (LLMDEndpoint) now add replicas on requests in flight per replica (targetInflight, default 16) instead of vLLM's waiting queue, so under steady load they scale out earlier than before. targetQueueDepth is ignored: if you tuned it, set targetInflight in the model's YAML.

The first apply in an account and region builds an EBS snapshot that holds the vLLM image, so GPU nodes start without downloading it. This makes the upgrade about 15 minutes longer, runs one temporary c5.xlarge and then costs about $1-2 a month of snapshot storage per vLLM version; the snapshot is kept when a cluster is destroyed. It needs kubectl on the machine that runs the upgrade. To skip it, set gpu_image_snapshot = false in your tfvars before upgrading.
The GPU EC2NodeClasses gain a snapshotID, so Karpenter marks existing GPU nodes as drifted. A node that runs model pods is not replaced while those pods run; it is replaced once it is empty.
